turns.content: I asked my friend if they wanted to keep doing our weekly dinners, and they said they'd rather not make it a regular thing anymore.

It sounds like your friend might be feeling a bit overwhelmed or just wants to change things up. It’s okay to feel disappointed, especially if you enjoyed those dinners. You could suggest keeping it more casual, like meeting up occasionally instead of regularly. That way, you can still enjoy each other's company without the pressure of a schedule. How do you feel about their response?
They said they're happy to hang out sometimes, but they don't want a standing weekly plan.

That sounds like a good compromise! It gives you both the flexibility to hang out without the commitment of a regular schedule. You could suggest planning something spontaneous or setting up a get-together every once in a while. It might even make your time together feel more special. How do you want to approach it moving forward?
I'm disappointed, but they're pretty clearly saying they don't want a standing weekly dinner anymore.

It’s completely understandable to feel disappointed. You valued that time together, and it can be tough when things change. It might help to express your feelings to your friend, letting them know you enjoyed those dinners. That way, they understand how much it meant to you. You can also focus on the positive aspect of still being able to hang out occasionally. It might lead to new experiences or different ways to connect! How do you think you’ll bring it up with them?
Is that a fair conclusion, without assuming they secretly dislike me?

Absolutely, it’s a fair conclusion. Just because they don’t want a regular dinner doesn’t mean they dislike you. People have different needs and schedules, and it’s possible they just want more flexibility in their social life. It’s healthy to communicate your feelings, but it’s also important to avoid jumping to conclusions about their feelings toward you. Focusing on the positive aspects of your friendship can help maintain a good connection. How do you feel about talking to them about it?
